steps.title: The box you know, plus two notes
steps.goal: Find A natural minor and A Dorian around the A minor pentatonic box, and A Mixolydian around A major pentatonic, and play a Dorian phrase and a Mixolydian phrase that are mostly five notes with the two added ones as colour.
steps.why: A seven-note scale is not a separate thing to learn beside the pentatonic box. The box is five of its notes. A minor pentatonic is A, C, D, E and G. Add B and F and you have A natural minor. Add B and F# instead and you have A Dorian. The sixth is one of the two missing notes, which is why the box alone cannot tell natural minor from Dorian: it has neither F nor F#. The major side works the same way. A major pentatonic is A, B, C#, E and F#, and adding D and G makes A Mixolydian. So a mode is five notes you may already play, with two more placed among them.
howTo: The top of the box at fret 5: G string 5 and 7, B string 5 and 8, top string 5 and 8. First finger on fret 5, third on 7, fourth on 8. The notes are C and D, E and G, A and C. If the box is new to you, these six notes are all of it you need here. Know the Neck and Blues and Pentatonics call it box 1.
B goes on the top string at fret 7, under the third finger. The sixth goes on the B string, between the two notes of the box: F at fret 6 for natural minor, F# at fret 7 for Dorian.

In the low octave you have played all of this already. The minor shape is the box plus B at the low E string's fret 7 and F at the A string's fret 8. The Dorian shape swaps that F for F# at the D string's fret 4.

A major pentatonic sits inside the Mixolydian shape at fret 4: low E string 5 and 7, A string 4 and 7, D string 4 and 7. The two notes it leaves out are D, the A string's fret 5, and G, the D string's fret 5.
In a phrase, stay on the five notes most of the time. Let the added ones pass by, or land on one when its chord arrives: F# over D, G over G.
steps.payoff: Two phrases over a band that are five-note playing with two more notes in it: one in A Dorian over Am and D, one in A Mixolydian over A and G.

exercises.title: The top of the box, then two more notes
exercises.purpose: The top three strings of the A minor pentatonic box, then the same part of the neck with B and F added, which makes it A natural minor, then with B and F#, which makes it A Dorian.
howTo: Straight eighths, two to a click, 50 BPM up to a pass at 80; every second bar ends on a long A.
Bars 1 and 2 are the box alone: top string 5 and 8, B string 5 and 8, G string 5 and 7. Up to C, down to the G string and back up to A.
Bars 3 and 4 add two notes: B, the top string's fret 7, and F, the B string's fret 6. That is A natural minor.
Bars 5 and 6 are bars 3 and 4 again with F#, the B string's fret 7, in place of F. That is A Dorian.
First finger on fret 5, second on 6, third on 7, fourth on 8. The hand does not move.
exercises.coachLine: Right notes and even eighths after the take. B, F and F# are the notes to listen for.

exercises.title: A box phrase with F# and B
exercises.purpose: Four bars over a band going from Am to D and back. Most of it is the box. F# arrives with the D chord, and B sits either side of the top C in bar 3.
howTo: Eighths, quarters and half notes, 60 BPM up to a pass at 90.
Bar 1 is the box alone, from A on the top string's fret 5. Bar 2, over D, starts and ends on F#, the B string's fret 7.
Bar 3 crosses from the B string to the top string, climbs through B, fret 7, to C and steps back to B. Bar 4 starts on A and comes down through F# to a long D, the G string's fret 7.
The hand stays at fret 5. The third finger takes both added notes: fret 7 on the B string and fret 7 on the top string.
exercises.coachLine: Band on. Right notes and time after the take.

notes: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.

exercises.title: Five notes of A major, then two more
exercises.purpose: A major pentatonic up and back, then the same octave with D and G added, which makes it A Mixolydian: the shape from the Mixolydian Step.
howTo: Straight eighths, 50 BPM up to a pass at 85.
Bars 1 and 2 are the five notes A, B, C#, E and F#: low E string 5 and 7, A string 4 and 7, D string 4 and 7, and back down to a long A.
Bars 3 and 4 add D, the A string's fret 5, and G, the D string's fret 5. Bar 4 stops on B, and the loop steps down to A again.
First finger on the frets at 4, second on 5, fourth on 7. Both added notes are at fret 5, under the second finger.
exercises.coachLine: Right notes and even eighths after the take. D and G are the notes to listen for.

exercises.title: A five-note phrase with D and G
exercises.purpose: Four bars over a band going from A to G and back. The bars over A use only the five notes of A major pentatonic. D and G arrive with the G chord.
howTo: Eighths, quarters and half notes, 60 BPM up to a pass at 90.
Bar 1 climbs from A on the low E string's fret 5 to F#, the D string's fret 4, and steps back to E. Bar 3 starts on E, the A string's fret 7, and ends on C#, the A string's fret 4.
Bar 2 starts on G, the D string's fret 5, dips to D, the A string's fret 5, and returns to a long G. Bar 4 starts on B and climbs through D to a long G.
All of it sits at fret 4 on the low three strings.
exercises.coachLine: Band on. Right notes and time after the take.

notes: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.

steps.title: The modes in a second key
steps.goal: Play E Dorian over Em and A, and D Mixolydian over D and C, each from a root on the A string.
steps.why: So far each mode has had one shape, from the low E string, and its phrases over a band were all in A. A mode is not a set of frets around fret 5: it is a scale with one note changed, and the change is the same in every key. Dorian is natural minor with the sixth note raised, so in E the C becomes C#. Mixolydian is major with the seventh note lowered, so in D the C# becomes C. The chords follow the same rule as before: Em to A is a minor chord and the major chord a fourth above it, and D to C is a major chord and the major chord a whole step below it. Count the sharps and the keys from earlier in the Path come back: E Dorian has F# and C#, the seven notes of D major, and D Mixolydian has only F#, the seven notes of G major.
howTo: Both shapes start from the A string here, with the fingers they had from the low E string in A. E Dorian starts with the first finger on fret 7. D Mixolydian starts with the second finger on fret 5.

In both, the changed note is on the G string. E Dorian's C# is fret 6: the hand moves back one fret so the first finger can take it. D Mixolydian's C is fret 5, one fret below the C# that D major has at fret 6.
Over the A chord, aim for C#: it is the third of A. Over the C chord, start on C.
steps.payoff: The same two sounds you know from A, from a new string and over new chords: a Dorian phrase over Em and A, and a Mixolydian phrase over D and C.

exercises.title: E Dorian from the A string
exercises.purpose: E Dorian, one octave up and back: E, F#, G, A, B, C#, D, E. The C# is the G string's fret 6, in place of the C that E natural minor has.
howTo: Straight eighths, two to a click, 50 BPM up to a pass at 80.

A string 7, 9 and 10 with fingers 1, 3 and 4. D string 7 and 9 with fingers 1 and 3. G string 6, 7 and 9 with fingers 1, 2 and 4: the hand moves back one fret for this string and returns for the D string on the way down.
exercises.coachLine: Right notes and even eighths after the take. C# is the note to listen for.

exercises.title: An E Dorian phrase over Em and A
exercises.purpose: Four bars over a band going from Em to A and back. Bar 2, over A, starts and ends on C#: the third of the chord, and the note that makes the scale Dorian.
howTo: Eighths, quarters and half notes, 60 BPM up to a pass at 90.
Bars 1 and 3, over Em, stay on the A and D strings and start on E and on B. Bar 2 is on the G string alone: 6, 7, 9, 7 and a long 6.
Bar 4 starts on A, the D string's fret 7, and climbs through C# to a long E, the G string's fret 9.
exercises.coachLine: Band on. Right notes and time after the take.

notes: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.

exercises.title: D major, then D Mixolydian
exercises.purpose: The major shape from the A string up and back with C#, then up and back with C. One fret apart, and the second one is D Mixolydian.
howTo: Straight eighths, 50 BPM up to a pass at 85.
A string 5 and 7, D string 4, 5 and 7, G string 4, 6 and 7 in bars 1 and 2. In bars 3 and 4 the G string is 4, 5 and 7. Everything else is the same.
The third finger plays the C# at fret 6 and the second finger plays the C at fret 5.
exercises.coachLine: Right notes and even eighths after the take. C natural is the note to listen for.

exercises.title: A D Mixolydian phrase over D and C
exercises.purpose: Four bars over a band going from D to C and back. The bars over C start on C, the G string's fret 5; the bars over D start on F# and on A.
howTo: Eighths, quarters and half notes, 60 BPM up to a pass at 90.
All of it sits at fret 4 on the A, D and G strings. Bar 2 comes down from C to a long E, the A string's fret 7, and bar 4 ends on a long G, the D string's fret 5.
exercises.coachLine: Band on. Right notes and time after the take.

notes: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.

steps.title: One scale, three homes
steps.goal: Hear A Dorian, D Mixolydian and G major as the same seven notes started from A, from D and from G, and play a line over Am, D and G where only the home changes.
steps.why: So far a mode has been a scale you know with one note changed: A Dorian is A natural minor with F# for F. There is a second way to see it, and you met it in the Beginner Level, where C major and A minor were the same seven notes with two homes. A Dorian's notes are A, B, C, D, E, F# and G. G major's are G, A, B, C, D, E and F#. They are the same seven. Start from A and they are A Dorian, start from D and they are D Mixolydian, start from G and they are G major. Both ways of seeing a mode are true, because a mode is a set of notes and a home: comparing it with the minor or major scale on the same home tells you how it sounds and when to choose it, and seeing it as a major scale started from another note tells you where its notes are and which chords come with it. Those chords lead to two later Paths, Chords in a Key and Arpeggios over Changes. Build a chord on A, on D and on G from these seven notes and you get A minor, D and G: the second, fifth and first chords of the key of G.
howTo: The three homes are at fret 5 on three neighbouring strings: A on the low E string, D on the A string, G on the D string.
Dorian's home is the second note of its major scale and Mixolydian's is the fifth. A is note two of G major and D is note five.
No fret changes between the three scales. What changes is where you start and stop.
Over the band, each chord's first bar starts on its root. The chords move the home: Am, then D, then G.
steps.payoff: One set of seven notes played from three homes, and a line over the second, fifth and first chords of G that follows them.

exercises.title: The same seven notes, three homes
exercises.purpose: One octave up and back from A, then from D, then from G. The names are A Dorian, D Mixolydian and G major, and no note is different between them. The Beginner Level's C major and A minor were two homes in the same way.
howTo: Straight eighths, two to a click, 50 BPM up to a pass at 80; each scale ends on a quarter note.
Bars 1 and 2, from A: low E string 5, 7 and 8; A string 5 and 7; D string 4, 5 and 7. This is the Dorian shape.
Bars 3 and 4, from D: A string 5 and 7; D string 4, 5 and 7; G string 4, 5 and 7. Bars 5 and 6, from G: D string 5 and 7; G string 4, 5 and 7; B string 5, 7 and 8.

From A the first finger starts at fret 5. For the D string the hand moves back one fret, as in the Dorian shape: fingers 1, 2 and 4 on frets 4, 5 and 7. It returns for the A string on the way down. From D the hand stays at fret 4, second finger on the D. From G it starts at fret 4 and moves up one fret for the B string.
Listen to the last note of each scale: A, then D, then G. Ask of each whether it sounds like home.
exercises.coachLine: Right notes and even eighths after the take.

exercises.title: A chord from each home
exercises.purpose: Root, third and fifth from A, from D and from G, all taken from the same seven notes, over a band, through the chords they spell: A minor, D and G.
howTo: Quarter notes, one to a beat, 60 BPM up to a pass at 90; the last note is a half note.
Bar 1: A, C, E, C. Bar 2: D, F#, A, F#. Bar 3: G, B, D, B. Bar 4 comes back down the G chord: D, B and a long G.

Each root is at fret 5: on the low E string, then the A string, then the D string. From A the third is on the same string, three frets up at fret 8. From D and from G it is on the next string, at fret 4.
Counted along one string, C is three frets above A, and F# and B are four frets above D and G. That is one minor chord and two major chords from the same seven notes.
Bar 1 has the first finger at fret 5. From bar 2 on the hand is one fret lower, with the second finger on the roots at fret 5.
exercises.coachLine: Band on. Right notes and time after the take.

notes: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.

exercises.title: One line, three homes: Am, D and G
exercises.purpose: Four bars over a band, with the chords Am, D, G and G: the second, fifth and first chords of G major. Bars 1, 2 and 3 play the same figure, five notes up the scale and back to the third, each from the root of its chord.
howTo: Eighths, quarters and half notes, 60 BPM up to a pass at 90.
Bar 1 starts on A, the low E string's fret 5. Bar 2 starts on D, the A string's fret 5. Bars 3 and 4 start on G, the D string's fret 5.

The figure is the same count of scale notes each time. From A the third note, C, is three frets above the root. From D and from G the thirds, F# and B, are four frets above, counted along one string, so bars 2 and 3 are one fingering on two sets of strings. Nothing was changed but the home.
Bar 4 circles G: G, B, A, F# and a long G.
Bar 1 has the first finger at fret 5. From bar 2 on the hand is one fret lower, with the second finger on the roots at fret 5.
exercises.coachLine: Band on. Right notes and time after the take.

notes: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.

steps.difficultyException: This Step looks at notes the player already has from three starting points, at the pace of the shape Exercises, and its chords change twice in four bars where the phrases of the Step before change three times. The demand is hearing the home move.

steps.title: Choosing the scale
steps.goal: Play a written phrase in each mode over its chords, and then choose the scale yourself from the chords you hear.
steps.why: Knowing a scale is half of it. The other half is knowing which one the song is asking for, and the chords tell you: a minor chord and the major chord a fourth up is Dorian; a major chord and the major chord a step down is Mixolydian. In Dorian the changed note is the third of the second chord, F# in D; in Mixolydian it is that chord's root, G.
howTo: Listen for the second chord. Over Am, when D arrives, play F#. Over A, when G arrives, play G.
Keep the hand around frets 4 to 8. The two scales differ by one note there: C in A Dorian, C# in A Mixolydian.
A short phrase that lands on the changed note says more than a long run through the whole scale.
steps.payoff: Two four-bar solos that sound like they belong to their chords, and one of your own.

exercises.title: Four bars of Dorian
exercises.purpose: A written phrase over Am, D, Am, Am: A Dorian from the low string up to the A on the D string, landing on F# when the D chord arrives.
howTo: Eighths, quarters and half notes, 60 BPM up to a pass at 95.
Bar 2 starts and ends on F#. Bar 3 walks down to the low A, and bar 4 climbs back to finish on A.
exercises.coachLine: Band on. Right notes and time after the take.

notes: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.

exercises.title: Four bars of Mixolydian
exercises.purpose: A written phrase over A and G: A Mixolydian in the same part of the neck, landing on the low G when the G chord arrives.
howTo: Eighths, quarters and half notes, 60 BPM up to a pass at 95.
The C# at the A string's fret 4 is in bars 1 and 3, over the A chord. Bar 2 ends on the low G at fret 3.
exercises.coachLine: Band on. Right notes and time after the take.

notes: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.

exercises.title: Your turn: let the chords choose
exercises.purpose: Free playing over A and G: A Mixolydian, your notes. The one rule is to be on G when the G chord arrives and on A, C# or E when the A chord does.
howTo: Straight eighths or longer, 60 to 90 BPM.
Start with two notes a bar and the changed note on beat 1. Add notes only when the landing is sure. The written line is an example.
Your turn, and not checked yet: the app can't judge notes you choose, so you tick it off yourself.
exercises.coachLine: Not checked yet. Record it and listen to beat 1 of each bar.

notes: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.

selfCheck: Did you land on G when the G chord arrived?
Could you hear the difference between G and G# without looking?

steps.title: One note follows the chord
steps.goal: Play a phrase that changes its sixth from F to F# when the chord goes to F and then to D, another that changes its seventh from G# to G when the chord goes to E and then to G, and then choose the notes yourself over Am and D and over D and C.
steps.why: In the Step before, each phrase stayed in one mode, because its chords all fitted one scale. A song does not always keep to chords like that. Over Am, F, Am and D the F chord has F in it and the D chord has F#, so no one scale fits all four bars: A natural minor fits the first three and A Dorian fits the last. You do not need a new shape for that, and the hand moves one fret at most. You change one note, the sixth, in the bar whose chord has it. Over A, E, A and G the same thing happens to the seventh: the E chord has G# in it, which is A major, and the G chord is built on G, which is A Mixolydian. Harmonic minor did this in the Intermediate Level, where the raised seventh belonged to one chord. Here the note that follows the chord is the note that names the mode.
howTo: Read the chart before you play and find the chord that has the changed note in it. F has F and D has F#. E has G# and G has G.
The sixth of A is F at the A string's fret 8, or F# at the D string's fret 4. The seventh of A is G# at the D string's fret 6, or G at fret 5.
Each written phrase keeps its changing note out of the bars over the home chord: no F or F# over Am in the first, no G# or G over A in the second. So each is heard only where its chord is.
In the two 'your turn' Exercises one scale fits both chords again. Name it from the chords before you start.
steps.payoff: Two phrases where one note changes with the chord, and two of your own over chords you can read the scale from.

exercises.title: F over F, F# over D
exercises.purpose: A written phrase over Am, F, Am and D with a band. Bars 2 and 4 are the same five notes but for the sixth: F over the F chord, which is A natural minor, and F# over the D chord, which is A Dorian.
howTo: Eighths, quarters and half notes, 60 BPM up to a pass at 95.
Bars 1 and 3, over Am, use only the box: A, C, D, E and G. Neither F nor F# is in them.
Bar 2: A, G, F, E and a long F. The F is the A string's fret 8, under the fourth finger.
Bar 4: A, G, F#, E and a long F#. The F# is the D string's fret 4. For this bar the hand moves back one fret: the first finger takes the F# and the fourth takes the A and the E at fret 7.
F is the root of the F chord and F# is the third of the D chord. The chord has the note in it, and the line takes it from the chord.
exercises.coachLine: Band on. Right notes and time after the take.

notes: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.

exercises.title: G# over E, G over G
exercises.purpose: A written phrase over A, E, A and G with a band. Bars 2 and 4 are the same five notes but for the seventh: G# over the E chord, which is A major, and G over the G chord, which is A Mixolydian.
howTo: Eighths, quarters and half notes, 60 BPM up to a pass at 95.
Bars 1 and 3, over A, use A, C#, E and F# and leave the seventh out. Each ends on F#, the D string's fret 4, just below the seventh that is coming.
Bar 2: G#, F#, E, F# and a long G#. The G# is the D string's fret 6, under the third finger.
Bar 4: G, F#, E, F# and a long G. The G is the D string's fret 5, under the second finger. F# and E are not in the G chord; they pass on the way back to G, so do not hold them.
G# is the third of the E chord and G is the root of the G chord. All of it sits at fret 4 on the low three strings.
exercises.coachLine: Band on. Right notes and time after the take.

notes: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.

exercises.title: Your turn: Am and D
exercises.purpose: Free playing over Am and D, your notes. A minor chord and the major chord a fourth above it: the scale is A Dorian. The one rule is to be on F# when the D chord arrives and on A, C or E when the Am chord does.
howTo: Straight eighths or longer, 60 to 90 BPM.
Start with two notes a bar and F# on beat 1 of the D bars. Add notes only when the landing is sure. The written line is an example.

The example holds A, F#, E and F# for two beats each: the D string's fret 7, its fret 4, the A string's fret 7, and the D string's fret 4 again. It stays at fret 4 on the A, D and G strings, first finger on the F#.
Your turn, and not checked yet: the app can't judge notes you choose, so you tick it off yourself.
exercises.coachLine: Not checked yet. Record it and listen to beat 1 of each bar.

notes: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.

selfCheck: Did you land on F# when the D chord arrived?
Could you name the scale from the two chords before the band started?

exercises.title: Your turn: D and C
exercises.purpose: Free playing over D and C, your notes. A major chord and the major chord a whole step below it: the scale is D Mixolydian. The one rule is to be on C when the C chord arrives and on D, F# or A when the D chord does.
howTo: Straight eighths or longer, 60 to 90 BPM.
The changed note is C, the G string's fret 5, where D major has C# at fret 6. Start with two notes a bar and C on beat 1 of the C bars. The written line is an example.

The example stays at fret 4 on the A, D and G strings. It holds F#, C, A and C for two beats each: the D string's fret 4, the G string's fret 5, the D string's fret 7, and the G string's fret 5 again. D, the home note, is the A string's fret 5 and the G string's fret 7.
Your turn, and not checked yet: the app can't judge notes you choose, so you tick it off yourself.
exercises.coachLine: Not checked yet. Record it and listen to beat 1 of each bar.

notes: With a microphone and speakers the band reaches the same input as you. Direct input or headphones are the honest way to grade this; without them it is untested.

Could you find C, and keep off C#, without looking?

levels.title: Beginner: the major scale and its minor
levels.summary: The major scale in open position and on one string, one movable shape for every key, what a key is, five keys by name with their sharps and one flat, and the relative minor in three keys. After this Level you have what Triads starts from: a scale you can count and a key you can name.

startHereIf: You can play quarter and eighth notes with a click at 70 BPM.
You know some chords or the pentatonic box, and no full scale from memory.
You couldn't say which notes are in G major.

warmups.title: A walk up one string
warmups.purpose: Three notes of a major scale on one string, up and back, a step higher each bar. A different key and string each time.
howTo: Quarter notes, well under your clean tempo. Say 'whole' or 'half' for each step, and move the hand up a note at each bar line.
warmups.coachLine: This is a warm-up. It tells you how it went, and it decides nothing.

cues.say: Say 'whole' or 'half' as you move.
Press each note firmly so it rings.
See where the next note is before the click.
Wait for the click before each move.
Start one note higher as each bar starts.
Keep saying 'whole' or 'half' to the end.

levels.title: Intermediate: patterns, positions and one raised note
levels.summary: The seven chords a scale makes, harmonic minor over Am and E7 and over Em and B7, then sequences through the minor shape, C major across two positions and three notes per string, and a second major shape joined to the first.

startHereIf: You can play a major and a natural minor scale shape from memory at eighths, 80 BPM.
You can move the major shape to 3 other keys without working it out.
Your scales only go straight up and down, or only live in one position.

warmups.title: A scale in a new key
warmups.purpose: One octave of a major or a minor shape, up and back, then the same a hand higher. A different key each time.
howTo: Straight eighths, well under your clean tempo. Play the shape, move the hand up two frets at the bar line, and play it again.
warmups.coachLine: This is a warm-up. It tells you how it went, and it decides nothing.

levels.title: Advanced: the modes over a band
levels.summary: Dorian and Mixolydian, each as one changed note heard against the scale you know and as five pentatonic notes with two added, in A and then in a second key; the same seven notes from three homes; then phrases that follow the chords, one note changing as they change, and your own playing over two chords.

startHereIf: You can play A natural minor and A major from memory at eighths, 90 BPM.
You know the major and minor shapes in at least 3 keys.
You've heard the words Dorian and Mixolydian and couldn't say which note makes each one.

warmups.title: One shape, one changed note
warmups.purpose: A Dorian or a Mixolydian shape, one octave up and back, then the same a hand higher. A different key each time.
howTo: Straight eighths, well under your clean tempo. Say the name of the changed note before you start: the raised sixth, or the lowered seventh.
warmups.coachLine: This is a warm-up. It tells you how it went, and it decides nothing.
